connections.observation: `s005` charts the progressive dissolution—softening, melting, pouring out, cutting—while `s008` stages this dissolution in two phases: beneficial softening (iron made χρήσιμον) followed by destructive continuation (enchantment producing μαλθακὸν αἰχμητήν). Held together, they make visible that the same process yields opposite outcomes depending on whether it stops at the right point or continues beyond it.

`s007` tracks θυμός/θυμοειδής as it undergoes softening, melting, weakening, and cutting; `s005` supplies the verbs of dissolution; `s009` supplies the μαλακ- family that names both the harmonies and the final state. Together they show that the soft harmonies enact on θυμός what their own adjective names, producing a μαλθακὸν warrior whose substance matches the music's quality.

`s001` names θυμοειδές and φιλόσοφον as the two natures that music and gymnastics address; `s003` tracks the ἁρμόζω family across the section; `s018` pairs the harmonized soul's virtues (σώφρων, ἀνδρεία) against the unharmonized soul's defects (δειλή, ἄγροικος). Held together, these make visible that harmonization is not abstract tuning but the concrete achievement of courage and moderation through the fitting adjustment of the two parts of nature.

`s002` contrasts ἀγριότης with ἡμερότης/μαλακότης; `s012` contrasts πειθώ through λόγοι with βία and ἀγριότης. Together they show that the ἄγριος quality named as one extreme reappears as the gymnastics-only person's operative mode: the noun becomes a manner of acting, savagery manifesting as reliance on force rather than persuasion.

`s004` corrects the common assumption (music for soul, gymnastics for body) to the claim that both are for the soul, body being πάρεργον; `s017` attributes the two arts to divine giving. Held together, they make visible that the god gave two arts not to address two entities (soul and body) but to address two aspects of one entity (θυμοειδές and φιλόσοφον within the soul).

`s011` presents music poured down through the ears as through a funnel while the person hums in delight; `s005` continues the pouring vocabulary (λείβει) as θυμός melts and is poured out. Together they show that the same downward pouring movement—first of harmonies into the soul, then of θυμός out of the soul—traces music's action from reception to dissolution.

`s006` cites three ὥσπερ similes: iron softened, sinews cut from the soul, person acting like a beast; `s005` supplies the verbs of softening and cutting. Together they make visible that the two educational failures are figured through opposed material transformations—iron made too soft versus the person made bestial—while both involve something essential being removed or lost.

`s013` tracks μουσική/Μοῦσα/ἄμουσος culminating in the gymnastics-only person becoming ἄμουσος; `s016` describes the φιλομαθές in that same person becoming ἀσθενές, κωφόν, and τυφλόν. Held together, these show that deprivation of the Muses is enacted as sensory deprivation: the ἄμουσος condition manifests as deafness and blindness in the soul's learning capacity.

`s010` contrasts χρήσιμον and ἀχρήστον at the moment iron-θυμός is beneficially softened; `s015` marks the threshold τοῦ δέοντος three times before replacing it with μέχρι τοῦ προσήκοντος. Together they make visible that usefulness depends on stopping at the right measure: the same process that makes iron χρήσιμον will make it ἄχρηστον if continued past τοῦ δέοντος.

`s014` concludes with string-tuning language (ἐπιτεινομένω, ἀνιεμένω, χορδάς) and mixing (κεραννύντα); `s003` has already used ἁρμόζω and συναρμόζω for the two natures. Held together, they show that the section moves from harmonization as abstract necessity to harmonization as concrete technical action—tightening and loosening music and gymnastics until the two natures sound together, surpassing mere string-tuning because the instrument is the soul.

`s007` tracks θυμός/θυμοειδής through softening, melting, cutting, and weakening; `s001` pairs θυμοειδές with φιλόσοφον as the two targets of education. Together they make visible an asymmetry: θυμοειδές is subjected to a detailed account of its vulnerability to excess, while φιλόσοφον receives briefer treatment, suggesting that the spirited part's susceptibility to deformation is the section's primary concern.

`s008` stages music's effect in two phases—beneficial softening, then destructive enchantment; `s015` marks τοῦ δέοντος three times as the threshold of excess. Together they make visible that the boundary between beneficial and destructive is not a change in kind but a continuation past the measure: enchantment (κηλῇ) is not a different action but the refusal to release (μὴ ἀνιῇ) after the proper point.

`s002` names ἀγριότης as the gymnastics-only excess; `s016` describes that person's φιλομαθές becoming κωφόν and τυφλόν; `s012` says that person no longer uses πειθώ through λόγοι but only βία. Held together, these show that savagery is not merely temperamental harshness but operates through specific deprivations: deafness to learning, blindness of perception, and the replacement of persuasive speech with force.

elements.context: οὗτος τὸ μὲν πρῶτον, εἴ τι θυμοειδὲς εἶχεν, ὥσπερ σίδηρον ἐμάλαξεν
ὅταν δʼ ἐπέχων μὴ ἀνιῇ ἀλλὰ κηλῇ, τὸ δὴ μετὰ τοῦτο ἤδη τήκει καὶ λείβει

new_signals.observation: τὸ μὲν πρῶτον and τὸ δὴ μετὰ τοῦτο ἤδη explicitly mark the two-stage temporal progression of music's action on θυμός: first softening, then melting.

elements.context: ἐὰν μέν γε, ἦν δʼ ἐγώ, ἐξ ἀρχῆς φύσει ἄθυμον λάβῃ, ταχὺ τοῦτο διεπράξατο
ὀξύρροπον ἀπηργάσατο, ἀπὸ σμικρῶν ταχὺ ἐρεθιζόμενόν τε καὶ κατασβεννύμενον

new_signals.observation: ταχύ recurs twice in adjacent lines: excessive music quickly completes its work on the naturally ἄθυμον person, while on the θυμοειδής person it produces a θυμός that is quickly roused and quickly extinguished.

elements.context: ἐὰν μέν γε, ἦν δʼ ἐγώ, ἐξ ἀρχῆς φύσει ἄθυμον λάβῃ
ἐὰν δὲ θυμοειδῆ, ἀσθενῆ ποιήσας τὸν θυμόν

new_signals.observation: ἄθυμον and θυμοειδῆ are contrasted as two starting natures that receive excessive music differently: the spiritless nature is quickly ruined, the spirited nature has its θυμός weakened into volatile irritability.

elements.context: οὐκ ἐπὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα, εἰ μὴ εἰ πάρεργον

new_signals.observation: πάρεργον appears as a strong qualification dismissing body as incidental to the purpose of music and gymnastics—not merely secondary but only relevant as a side-effect.
μαλθακὸν αἰχμητήν is an oxymoronic pair: a soft warrior, the contradiction naming the result of excessive music applied to θυμός.

elements.context: ἀπὸ σμικρῶν ταχὺ ἐρεθιζόμενόν τε καὶ κατασβεννύμενον

new_signals.observation: Two passive participles in parallel (roused and extinguished) describe the weakened θυμός as oscillating rapidly—a grammatical parallelism enacting the instability it names.
ἐγείρω recurs: the proper educator rouses (ἐγείρων) the θυμοειδές through exercise; the gymnastics-only person's φιλομαθές is never roused (οὐκ ἐγειρόμενον) because it receives no learning.
